subject: Tenant hardening & hosting lane sizing — private vs dedicated for regulated workloads
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@alderbio.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant hardening & hosting lane sizing — private vs dedicated for regulated workloads

Hi Jane,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Per our conversation, I wanted to capture a quick sizing question so we can align on hosting lanes (Redwood Private vs Dedicated reserved pools) and a rough onboarding timeline. You mentioned AlderBio needs a compliance-first posture for PHI-bearing inference traffic and a hard isolation requirement for certain model endpoints. A couple of clarifying items will help us produce a scoped proposal: 

- Expected steady-state QPS for the regulated endpoints (p95 over business hours). If you have concurrent session counts that’s helpful.
- Typical prompt size and expected response token length (avg).
- Peak burst multiple (e.g., 3x steady-state for day-of-week spikes).
- Any hard restrictions: air-gap/physical on-premise, minimum tenancy (single-tenant per customer), or restricted egress.

If you don’t have exact numbers, a best-effort ranges works (e.g., 20–50 qps steady, 150 qps peak). I’ll loop our deal engineering and product ops into next steps once we have these.

I’ve attached the mutual action plan template and our compliance checklist for quick reference.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: AlderBio_MA_requirements.pdf, mutual-action-plan-template.xlsx
From: Jane Sullivan <jane.sullivan@alderbio.com>

Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Tenant hardening & hosting lane sizing — private vs dedicated for regulated workloads

Marcus — thank you. Quick answers below to get you started: 

- Steady-state (regulated endpoints): ~35 qps p95 during business hours (M–F 8am–6pm PT).
- Concurrent sessions: typically 25–40 active sessions for the regulated feature set.
- Avg prompt/response: ~120 tokens in, ~450 tokens out (we use long-form summarization).
- Peak: we see spikes up to ~3.5x on release days (so plan for ~125 qps burst).
- Restrictions: Must be single-tenant for the regulated model endpoints; data cannot leave customer-controlled VPC in certain regions (ideally VPC peering to Redwood Private control plane or on-prem). No requirement for full air-gap today, but legal will ask about the option.

We also need SOC2 evidence and a sample SOW to accelerate procurement — cc’ing procurement@alderbio.com.

Best,
Jane Sullivan
Head of AI Product, AlderBio Health
jane.sullivan@alderbio.com

Jane / procurement — thanks for the quick detail and the SOC2 ask; procurement noted. I’m looping Priyom (deal engineering) and Marissa (product ops) to validate resource sizing and propose an onboarding lane.

Priyom/Marissa — AlderBio is asking for single-tenant isolation for regulated endpoints with expected steady-state ~35 qps and up to 125 qps burst; avg request/response tokens ~120/450. They prefer traffic to remain in a customer-controlled VPC or a peered network. Legal may ask about air-gap options but not mandatory today.

Immediate asks for the team:
- Quick sizing calc (GPU counts for dedicated reserved vs Private on-prem equivalent + rough cost delta).
- Onboarding timeline (security review, network peering/VPN, SOC evidence, SSO + key management).
- Any constraints we should flag for procurement (lead times for reserved capacity, specialized hardware procurement).

I attached our SOW draft (SOW-draft-v2.docx) — can we aim to return a recommended option by EOD Friday to keep the procurement cadence moving?

Thanks — Marcus
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Looping in sizing + deployment ops — AlderBio requirements

Folks — did a rapid sizing pass and included assumptions up front. Attaching a short XLS (inference-sizing-calcs.xlsx) with the line-item math. Summary below: 

Assumptions (from thread): 35 qps steady p95; peak 125 qps; avg response 450 tokens; average generation latency target p95 = 600ms. We assume model = 70B opt-quantized variant (latency profile similar to current 70B quant runs).

Option A — Dedicated reserved (single-tenant GPU pool, Redwood-managed infra):
- Effective throughput per A100-80GB equiv (with batching and KV cache): ~6–8 qps at p95 for long-form 450-token outputs given our latency target.
- Recommended baseline: 6 x A100-80GB GPUs (handles ~36–48 qps steady with headroom).
- Peak/burst plan: Autoscale + burst to an additional 4 GPUs (soft limit) to cover 125 qps short-lived spikes.
- Notes: Faster time-to-live (no on-prem procurement), SLA on availability, lower procurement friction.

Option B — Private (VPC-hosted tenant or on-prem single-tenant):
- Baseline: 9–12 x A100-80GB (or equivalent Ampere instances) given additional overheads (network isolation, locked-down orchestration, lower batch packing early in life).
- Burst: additional 6 GPUs for peak coverage if customer cannot burst to hosted.
- Notes: Higher baseline to compensate for lower packing and initial cold-cache; stronger control plane isolation (can support VPC peering), longer procurement and set-up (~8–12 weeks if on-prem hardware).

Cost delta: Private baseline ~1.6–2.0x the committed-cost of Dedicated reserved (depends on hardware selection and provisioning model).

Risk considerations: On-prem introduces procurement lead times and longer onboarding; dedicated reserved has faster ramp and operational support, but requires contractual tenant isolation guarantees (we can provide dedicated pools per customer).

Action items I recommend we present to AlderBio: 1) Dedicated reserved proposal for pilot with clear SLA and isolation guarantees (quicker), 2) Parallel project plan for Private tenancy if AlderBio wants VPC-only footprint for regulated endpoints — includes procurement milestones and network runbook.

Priyom
Deal Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Looping in sizing + deployment ops — AlderBio requirements

Thanks — quick ops notes to add color for procurement and onboarding timelines: 

- Hybrid lane (recommended): Offer a Private control plane with dedicated GPU pools for the regulated model endpoints. This lets us keep control-plane telemetry in Redwood while ensuring compute is single-tenant and VPC-peered. For the pilot (4–6 weeks) we can carve a smaller dedicated reserved pool (6 GPUs) to validate latency and caching behavior, then scale to the private baseline if isolation testing passes.
- Networking: VPC peering + strict route tables, optional customer-controlled NAT for egress. Require one-week network window for peering + firewall rules testing.
- Keys & encryption: Recommend KMS integration (customer-managed keys) — takes ~2 weeks to validate.
- Onboarding timeline (pilot -> full): Pilot deployment & validation (4–6 weeks), Security/Compliance sign-off (2–4 weeks parallel), Production scale/procurement (6–10 weeks if hardware purchase needed).
- Procurement flag: If AlderBio insists on on-prem hardware, include long lead-time clause (12–18 weeks) and acceptance testing milestones.

I’ll draft a short two-option SOW (pilot on dedicated reserved vs private baseline) and send it by EOD Tuesday.

-Marissa
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Looping in sizing + deployment ops — AlderBio requirements

Looping in security considerations from the compliance team: 

- SOC2 evidence: we can provide the standard SOC2 Type II pack. For customer-specific audit requests (e.g., control mappings), allow 5 business days for our security team to produce tailored evidence.
- Audit logs & retention: For regulated endpoints we recommend 13 months retention of request/response metadata by default, but we can support custom retention policies tied to the Private tenant.
- Key management: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private lanes; for Dedicated reserved we can support CMK with limited key escrow as part of the contract.
- Network isolation: VPC peering + mTLS for control-plane traffic; if AlderBio requires physical air-gap options, we’ll need a follow-up with infra procurement (this is a separate engagement and materially increases timeline and cost).

I’ll attach a short checklist for procurement (SOC2 excerpts, control mappings, encryption matrix).

- Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

2) SOC2 pack + short control mapping doc (for our legal).
3) Mutually agreed MAP with milestones for the pilot -> private decision gate.

Can the team deliver the SOW + docs by Monday EOD? If yes we’ll route to legal and procurement for signature.

Thanks — Jane
